subject: Beijer et al. (2019)
object: In affected members of 3 unrelated families with juvenile-onset autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to identify heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin.

subject: Beijer et al. (2019)
object: Beijer et al. (2019) reported 3 families with juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by SPTAN1 nonsense mutations. Penetrance was variable in 2 of the 3 families, and the severity of the phenotype differed greatly between patients.

subject: Beijer et al. (2019)
object: In patient cells, Beijer et al. (2019) found that mutant SPTAN1 mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and that alpha-II spectrin protein levels were reduced. This contrasts with the dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations previously described as causing a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.

subject: Ylikallio et al. (2020)
object: Ylikallio et al. (2020) reported a de novo SPTAN1 mutation associated with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy and a developmental disorder.

subject: Dong et al. (2021)
object: Dong et al. (2021) reported a novel de novo nonsense variant in the SPTAN1 gene that caused hereditary motor neuropathy in a Chinese family.
